need: Frontend UX flow design must explicitly compare page, modal, drawer, popover, and inline presentation for every meaningful interaction, then preserve the approved decision through UI detail, implementation, responsive behavior, and UAT.
negativeBoundary: Do not default every interaction to a page or inline card, prioritize overlays for novelty, infer the container from existing components, hide a primary journey inside an overlay, or approve UAT without proving actual container behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: UX flow cannot reach review until every meaningful interaction has one selected container and explicit rejection reasons for the four alternatives.
Modal is limited to a short bounded blocking decision; drawer is limited to contextual secondary work that preserves page context.
Every overlay declares dismissal, focus return, background behavior, and constrained-viewport transformation.
UI detail binds each approved container to exact trigger and surface ownership without silently replacing it.
Product UAT proves actual container identity, dismissal or back behavior, focus return, and mobile transformation in the running product.

accepts: Container selection based on task semantics and responsive behavior.
Explicit consideration of modal and drawer where their interaction jobs fit.
rejects: A beautiful user story whose flow silently renders every interaction as a page or card.
A modal or drawer chosen only because the component exists or looks modern.

review.rationale: Approved after state-machine, operator, UI-detail, and product-UAT contracts made interaction-container comparison and proof mandatory, with four focused regression cases covering invalid modal, drawer, and alternative-selection behavior.
